findings.reason: naming the owner turns §9's detector into an extension of measure_context_budget (which today counts only boundary records, not the consecutive `system/status: compacting` rows shape 5 is made of) instead of a new reader that will drift from it.
findings.text: §9's measure proposes dispatch "detects shape 5 from the stream as N compacting records with no boundary within T seconds", but measure_context_budget in this file already opens the run stream and parses its compaction records (with a compaction record type constant `system/compact_boundary` at context_budget.py:26, counting boundaries and reading compact_metadata.pre_tokens), and the plan cites neither it nor death_census.py, so it does not show it searched before proposing a second stream parser.

findings.reason: the deep shape is one reader with an arm per shape (death_census.classify at death_census.py:128 already returns completed/dead/running from one pair of facts), which deletes the per-shape detectors rather than adding them.
findings.text: §9 says "each remaining death shape gets a harness-level prevention" and lists inherited-session, compaction-threshold and bounded-turn handlers, each re-reading the stream for its own signal, rather than one classification pass whose result names the honest recovery; that the plan itself enumerates five death shapes at §9's own comment (killed mid-thinking, first-turn refusal, compaction-never-completes) makes the spread five detectors over one stream.

findings.reason: §9 should state the compaction threshold as a derived value of the single effective-window figure, or justify the second key; two independent keys for one wall can be set apart so a caller sets one while the refusal check reads the other — the divergence §7 exists to close.
findings.text: §9's prevention candidate "a compaction threshold set below the effective boundary" adds a second tunable for the lane's input wall beside the effective_input_window slot §7 landed in the flight schema, and does not say why that one declaration cannot carry the threshold.

findings.reason: the compaction shape belongs as one more block in the existing stream observer and one more arm of classify_pointer/death_census; a parallel classifier is the ordering fork §3's own lock at recovery.py already guards against, and it will read a run through a different path than the sweep does.
findings.text: §9's "dispatch detects shape 5 ... and ends the run as its own classification. Recovery then starts a fresh session" re-implements terminal-shape classification: death_census.classify already reads a run's terminal stream for the result record and process liveness, and recovery.classify_pointer already consumes per-shape blocks the stream observer writes (_stream_budget recovery.py:4722, _stream_refusal_block recovery.py:4742, _stream_exhaustion_block recovery.py:4777), so a dispatch-side shape-5 classifier forks the reading.

findings.reason: the comment does give a reason the project-wide key cannot serve — the rule must travel with the run across coordinator restarts — so this refines the node rather than redirecting it; the placement correction is to record the constraint inside the same candidate composer, which the plan can take as a note, not a rewrite.
findings.text: §4's per-run `local_only` constraint (comment c-20260923T1345) adds a second review-lane-selection input beside the existing review_excluded_backends flight key (recovery.py:1199, _review_excluded_backends recovery.py:2010) and `_review_lane_candidates`, which already composes the review lane from the owning run's recorded backend.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §9's "each remaining death shape gets a harness-level prevention" spreads one classification concern across a handler per shape rather than one deep classifier whose interface answers how a run ended.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §9 re-implemented by name: its shape-5 detection duplicates context_budget.py's compaction parser and its "ends the run as its own classification" duplicates death_census.classify / recovery.classify_pointer.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §9 adds a dispatch-side compaction-shape detector and per-shape preventions without citing reckon/crew/context_budget.py or reckon/crew/death_census.py, the modules that already parse compaction records and terminal stream shape.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §9's "compaction threshold set below the effective boundary" layers a second tunable over the effective-window declaration landed in §7 with no reason that declaration cannot carry it.
